attempted_axis: First record on this function (zero-record row of the run-41 near-miss re-rank, real 83 at T149/O150). attributes.law_screen: claim.law.declaration-initializer-split-controls-entry-schedule.20260830.v1 APPLIED as probe 1's whole premise and MEASURED NOT APPLICABLE HERE: splitting `char* strs = (char*)lbl_80115DA8;` into a bare declaration plus a first-statement assignment left the object BYTE-IDENTICAL (probe.py NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL, PROOF bytes=2ecd97842a85), so on this function the split does not reach the entry schedule at all - the law's mechanism is real elsewhere but does not cover an ADDR16_LO hoisted across the prologue. claim.law.declaration-order-numbers-the-registers-assignment-order-schedules-the-loads.20260901.v1 APPLIED and CONFIRMED in both directions: probe 2 (declaration moved last) changed the object and made it much worse, probe 3 (assignment moved last) changed the object without touching the prologue at all - i.e. declaration order decides the callee-saved home, statement order does not reach it, exactly as the law states. claim.law.identical-multiset-is-blind-to-displacements.20260831.v1 SCREENED, not applicable (the multiset DIFFERS). claim.law.constant-copy-vs-rematerialize-is-source-unreachable.20260831.v1 SCREENED, not applicable (an address materialisation split across the prologue, not two locals sharing a constant). core-screen offsetof/lwzu/index laws: none applicable.
attributes.probed_form:
BASELINE real 83, insns T149/O150, multiset 1t. Target prologue: `mflr r0 ; lis r3,@lbl_80115DA8(HA) ; stw r0,4(r1) ; stwu r1,-32(r1) ; stmw r26,8(r1) ; addi r31,r3,@lbl_80115DA8(LO)`. Ours: `mflr r0 ; lis r3,HA ; stw r0,4(r1) ; addi r0,r3,LO ; lis r3,@lbl_802A5CF0(HA) ; stwu r1,-32(r1) ; addi r4,r3,LO ; stmw r26,8(r1) ; mr r31,r0` - both hoist the `lis`, ours additionally hoists the `addi`, and r31 is not yet saved at that point, so it lands in r0 and needs the copy.
PROBE 1 (NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL, decisive at one): split the declaration from its initialiser --
        char* strs;                       /* was `char* strs = (char*)lbl_80115DA8;` */
        ...
        strs = (char*)lbl_80115DA8;       /* first statement of the body */
Object bytes unchanged; initialiser and first-statement assignment are the same construct to the front end.
PROBE 2 (REGRESSED real 83 -> 151): move the declaration to the END of the declaration list (after `u8* h;`). This DOES reach codegen and is much worse, which proves `strs` must be declared FIRST to hold r31 - i.e. the register assignment is already the target's and only the hoist is wrong.
PROBE 3 (NEUTRAL-REARRANGED, prologue UNCHANGED): keep the declaration first, move the assignment to last of the four opening assignments --
        background = (MboxBackgroundState*)lbl_802A5CF0;
        index = lbl_80344E88;
        models = gWinGlobals;
        strs = (char*)lbl_80115DA8;
Object bytes moved elsewhere but `addi r0,r3,LO` stayed at +0xc and `mr r31,r0` at +0x20; the aligned prologue view is byte-for-byte the same as the baseline's.
All three reverted; the tree is back at the baseline (real 83).
attributes.residual: One instruction, `mr r31,r0` at +0x20. This is the project's recurring EAGER PRE-PROLOGUE ADDRESS RESOLUTION class - the same shape recorded (with negative outcomes) on game/boss/bosscam::TriggerCamUpdate (attempt.triggercamupdate-eager-sda21-prologue-negative.20260830.v1) and game/boss/bosscam::TriggerCameraActivate (attempt.parked.triggercameraactivate.20260829.v1), both of which carry UNGATED-PROSE denials rather than typed ones. hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: One probe. Move `u8* indexed;` to directly after `char* strs;` and re-run `python tools/gdl/probe.py game/mb/mb_model MBOX_BGLoadModelDone`. If `indexed` still lands in a volatile register, or lands in r30 while `addi r0,r3,LO` stays at +0xc, the pressure reading is wrong and the function should be typed-parked as an eager-pre-prologue candidate together with the two bosscam instances.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes - the aligned `fnasm game/mb/mb_model MBOX_BGLoadModelDone 0x0:0x50 --diff` view at HEAD shows target `add r30,r4,r0` / `lwz r0,728(r30)` against our `add r7,r4,r0` / `lwz r0,728(r7)`, which is the observation the hypothesis is built on; the declaration move itself has NOT been compiled.
hypothesis.statement: The hoist is a symptom of entry-block register pressure, not of how `strs` is spelled: the target keeps `indexed` in the callee-saved r30 (`add r30,r4,r0` at +0x40) while ours puts it in the volatile r7 (`add r7,r4,r0`), so our entry block has one fewer callee-saved home in play and MWCC schedules the free ADDR16_LO into the pre-prologue slot. The untried lever is therefore on `indexed`, not `strs`: move `u8* indexed;` up in the declaration list so it takes r30, and re-measure whether the `addi` for `strs` sinks below `stmw` on its own.
